title: Stability Weave Initiative: cross-team ops protocols and SLO rollout plan
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the operational protocols, cross-functional milestones, and runbook commitments for the "Stability Weave" initiative — a coordinated push to establish service-level objectives, standardized observability, and a staged rollout pattern for model-serving and control-plane features across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. This is a working plan: expect gaps, TODOs and open questions.

High-level goals (Q1–Q2):
- Define litmus SLOs for token-latency (p50/p95/p99), request success, and model-quality regression (as measured by eval set pass-rate).
- Create standardized dashboards and alert thresholds per SLI with templated Grafana/Lightstep panels.
- Ship a canary + staged rollout pattern for model swaps with automated fallback to lower-cost variants.
- Onboard 5 feature teams into the SLO program and run a 90-day experiment.

Scope and assumptions:
- Focus starts on serving-runtime and routing layers, then expands to console and customer-facing SLAs.
- Private deployments: provide runbook templates and KMS/HSM integration checks, but not full automation for air-gapped installs in this phase.
- We assume platform telemetry retention of 30 days for trial; needs extension for production.

Key deliverables and owners:
1) SLO taxonomy & measurable SLIs (owner: Miguel Torres) — deliver by 2026-02-28
   - Draft SLI definitions (latency buckets, error class mapping, model-quality signal definitions)
   - Mapping to existing telemetry metrics and synthetic probes
2) Observability templates (owner: Sofia Kim) — deliver dashboards + alerting templates by 2026-03-12
   - Grafana dashboards, alert policies (PagerDuty + email), Lightstep traces examples
3) Canary rollout recipe (owner: Evelyn Zhang) — deliver automated pipeline + runbook by 2026-03-31
   - Describe traffic split cadence, success criteria, rollback thresholds, data retention during canary
4) Runbooks & escalation matrix (owner: Tom Briggs) — deliver runbooks + oncall playbook by 2026-03-15
   - Triage checklist, runbook snippets for common faults (KV cache blowup, OOM, model mismatch), Slack bridge templates
5) Team onramp program (owner: Asha Patel) — training + 5-team pilot schedule by 2026-04-15

Milestones and cadence:
- Weekly working sync (platform-engineering + serving-runtime + SRE): Tue 10:30am PST, outcomes tracked in JIRA-REL-2027
- Biweekly cross-functional review with Product/Console: alternate Thursdays
- End-of-phase demo: 2026-04-22 (show SLO dashboards + canary run)

Operational rules & gating:
- A feature is eligible for staged rollout only after: SLI instrumentation added, unit-level synthetic test passing for 7 days, and preflight cost/latency benchmark recorded.
- Canary success criteria (example): p95 latency within 1.2x baseline AND error-rate not increased beyond 0.5% absolute AND model-quality delta <= 1% on eval set.
- If any criterion fails for two consecutive windows, automated rollback and notify oncall channel (#reliability-weave).

Monitoring/Alerting specifics:
- Alerts should be tiered: page (P1) for hard availability degradations, page (P2) for sustained p99 degradation or error spikes, and email-only for minor regressions in model-quality signals.
- PagerDuty run duration: 30 min escalation to secondary, 90 min to SRE lead.

Canary template (copyable):
- Phase 0: 100 synthetic requests/sec to canary variant for 2 hours; compare traces and metrics to baseline (automated job).
- Phase 1: 1% traffic for 3 hours, monitor SLOs + model-quality; require green for 3 windows.
- Phase 2: 10% traffic for 6 hours, require green for 4 windows.
- Phase 3: gradual ramp to 50% with continuous monitoring and optional manual guardrail.

Training & comms:
- Create a 45-minute recording + quick reference sheet for SLO authors: how to write an SLI, how thresholds map to alerts, and troubleshooting common errors. (Owner: Asha)
- Slack channel: #reliability-weave for async ops, #reliability-weave-ops for oncall pings.
- Knowledge base: Confluence page CONFLUENCE-5543 will host canonical runbooks and examples.

Risk register (top items):
- Telemetry gaps: missing histograms for token-level latency in some stacks. Mitigation: add lightweight agent-based sampling.
- False positives on model-quality alerts during downstream data drift. Mitigation: maintain rolling baselines and add drift detector.
- Cross-team bandwidth: platform and product sprints collide. Mitigation: lock minimal acceptance criteria and prioritize pilot teams.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What retention period for model-quality time-series is acceptable for long-term regressions? (ops budget vs. investigability)
- Should Private deployment runbooks include a mandatory dry-run with customer infra? (legal/PS input required)
- Define exact alert thresholds for p99 across small bursty services — do we standardize percent delta vs absolute ms?

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Miguel: share SLI draft and metric mapping (due 2026-01-20) — links to JIRA-REL-2027-1
- Sofia: spin up dashboard scaffold and link to synthetic job (due 2026-01-22)
- Evelyn: prototype canary job in staging (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/PR#784)
- Tom: assemble runbook skeleton and escalate to SRE lead for review (due 2026-01-25)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a "quality shadow" mode where new model variant runs in parallel with production and records outputs without serving customers (useful for eval drift).
- Add small daily cost estimate of canary runs to cost dashboard so Finance can audit incremental spend.

References and links:
- CONFLUENCE-5543 (SLO templates and history)
- JIRA-REL-2027 (initiative epic)
- PR#784 (staging canary pipeline prototype)
- Slack: #reliability-weave

Versioning and archival:
- This doc will be iterated in place until pilot completion. Finalized playbooks will be exported to Confluence and archived under "reliability/playbooks" with version tags.

Appendix: runbook snippets (scratch)
- If KV cache eviction spike: check mem-usage, restart worker pool with reduced parallelism, patch config token-per-worker to limit requests, notify platform oncall.
- If model mismatch errors (shape/weights): rollback to previous model variant via rollout API, inform model-onboarding owner, run anti-entropy job.

Feedback / edits: add inline or leave comments in Confluence-5543, or ping Asha/Ash on Slack.
